statement: Memory manufacturers are prioritizing higher-margin HBM and server-grade DDR5 and cutting standard DDR4/embedded output, with new fabrication capacity not online until late 2026 - conditions that may persist into 2027.
why: Reallocation of memory capacity toward HBM and server DDR5 tightens whole-chain memory supply for standard parts and concentrates output on AI-grade memory.

impact.mechanism: Prioritizing HBM/server DDR5 favors GPU-attached memory supply (supportive for accelerators) while starving standard DRAM, keeping overall memory supply tight until new capacity arrives late 2026.

evidence.excerpt: Memory manufacturers are prioritizing higher-margin products, such as HBM and server-grade DDR5, reducing output for standard DDR4 and embedded-focused parts, with new memory fabrication capacity not expected to come online until late 2026, meaning current conditions may persist into 2027.

confidence.basis: Secondary: TechTimes via web-search index, corroborated by an independently fetched source (ComparetheCloud); two publishers, capped at medium.
